Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and congrats on the usage milestone. We can support a split payment for the prorated add-on. Proposed approach below so your procurement/finance can confirm: 

Option A (recommended): Redwood issues two invoice documents tied to a single SOW: 
- Invoice INV-20261108-ACME-1 (50% of prorated add-on) due on receipt
- Invoice INV-20261108-ACME-2 (remaining 50%) due in 30 days

We will calculate VAT on each invoice at the point of issuance (since Acme has an EU VAT ID, VAT should be applied according to reverse charge rules — we'll mark the invoice accordingly, but we need a copy of your VAT registration to support this).

Merchant fees: payments processed via our Stripe account incur per-transaction processing fees. Stripe charges are applied to Redwood; by default these are not passed back as a separate line item to customers. However, for split payments it increases our processing cost because it multiplies the number of transactions. We can: 
- Option 1: Redwood absorbs the incremental processing fee for this one-time request (no extra line item).
- Option 2: Redwood issues the invoices as-is and adds a small processing surcharge as a separate line (typically a flat €10 per extra transaction).

If you confirm Option A and indicate whether you prefer Redwood to absorb the fee or accept a €10 processing line, we'll generate the two invoices and a short DocuSign SOW for signature. Please also send the PO number and a copy of the VAT registration.

Action items: 
- Sarah: confirm split (50/50) and processing fee preference, send PO and VAT reg copy
- Laura/Monica: once I have confirmation I will ask Billing to generate INV-20261108-ACME-1 and INV-20261108-ACME-2 and set payment terms

From: mateo@stripe.com (Mateo Cruz)
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, billing@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 07:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Split payment flow + VAT implications

Hi all — quick note from payments: Stripe will charge processing fees per successful charge; there is no built-in multi-charge discount. If you create two charges for the same order there will be two fee events. 

On VAT: VAT handling depends on where the merchant is registered and where the supply is considered delivered. For EU VAT-registered buyers using reverse charge, the supplier (Redwood) should include the buyer's VAT number and the reverse charge annotation on the invoice at issuance. VAT does not get 'held back' by Stripe — it's an invoicing/legal treatment.

Also: consider a single invoice with a payment schedule (two due dates) rather than two separate invoices if you want to minimize bookkeeping complexity; Stripe supports multiple scheduled payments against a single invoice via hosted invoice payments or PaymentIntent scheduling. That would generate a single invoice number and still allow split capture, reducing the extra transaction count in bookkeeping but technically Stripe will still process each capture as a separate card/ACH transaction (and fees still apply per capture).

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to talk technical implementation.

Mateo Cruz
